root_cause: (1) parseStructured accepted any string as the subject pubkey of leave_intent / invite_cancelled (typeof === 'string'); ChatBox feeds the subject to pubkeyToNpub -> nip19.npubEncode, which throws on non-hex, so one crafted member message broke the timeline render for every receiver. The existing member_admitted / invite_lifecycle regex guard also had a latent hole: RegExp#test coerces its argument, so a one-element array ["<64 hex>"] passed. (2) profileSync.payloadToMemberProfile stored any avatar.imageUrl (javascript:, data:, http: trackers, unbounded length) while the 1:1 dmProfile codec enforced https:// or // and a 512-char cap.
fix: parseStructured.ts: one isCanonicalPubkey guard (typeof string AND /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/) applied to every subject-carrying announcement (leave_intent, invite_cancelled, member_admitted, invite_lifecycle). dmProfile/kinds.ts: extracted the avatar URL rules into exported avatarImageUrlProblem()/isAllowedAvatarImageUrl() + exported AVATAR_IMAGE_URL_MAX_LENGTH; the 1:1 encoder and parser now use it with identical reasons/throw messages (1:1 behaviour unchanged). profileSync.ts: payloadToMemberProfile keeps the avatar only if the (direct or legacy-id-reconstructed) imageUrl passes isAllowedAvatarImageUrl; otherwise avatar=null and nickname/updatedAt/signedEvent/pubkey are kept. Actor-only fields that are never rendered (invite_cancelled.by, poll_open.creatorPubkey, call_notice.initiator) deliberately left as-is: renderers attribute from the protocol-authenticated sender.

tests_added.kinds: parameterized malformed-subject rejection for all 6 subject-carrying announcement shapes; seeded-PRNG property tests (no fast-check in repo): 'parses iff subject matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ and a parsed subject always npub-encodes', 'group sync keeps the avatar iff the shared 1:1 predicate accepts the URL (nickname always kept)'; avatar drop cases (javascript:, data:, http:, ftp:, relative, whitespace, oversize, non-string, invalid legacy id); predicate boundary at 512.
